extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from primary text/figures and supplementary figure captions; direct assay classes are kept bounded to the reported assays.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The peptides support membrane disruption/permeabilization mechanisms in bacteria, based on TEM morphology, cytoplasmic membrane potential changes, and PI uptake assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: 1-4, S-4, L-4, and P-4 across the tested bacteria where each figure panel applies

supports: Figure 6/methods report TEM, membrane-potential, and PI membrane-damage assays

mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure-level quantitative values are not converted into per-peptide numeric mechanism rows unless available in text; claim is qualitative direct-mechanism evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The peptides are supported as causing DNA damage/degradation in tested bacteria and oxidative damage in L. monocytogenes, based on genomic DNA gel and DCFH-DA fluorescence assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: 1-4, S-4, L-4, and P-4 in the bacteria shown in Figure 7 and supplementary figures

supports: Figure 7 and supplementary captions report genomic DNA degradation and DCFH-DA staining assays

mechanism_claims.limitations: Claim is limited to the directly imaged/tested conditions; no exact band-density or fluorescence values are fabricated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The peptides show rapid bacterial penetration/colocalization with nucleic-acid staining in tested bacteria, supporting the paper claim of membrane-penetrating hybrid peptides.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: TMR-1-4 and reported peptide class in colocalization assays

supports: Figure 5 and Figure S4 captions report TMR-1-4 colocalization with DAPI-stained bacteria over time

mechanism_claims.limitations: The direct assay is fluorescence localization; downstream antibacterial mechanism still requires the separate membrane/DNA/ROS assays above.
